notes.definition: The test for carbon dioxide uses limewater, which is an aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide. When carbon dioxide is shaken with or bubbled through limewater, the limewater turns milky (cloudy).
explanation: Limewater is a clear, colourless solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂, in water. To test a gas for carbon dioxide, bubble the gas through limewater using a delivery tube, or shake a test tube of the gas with a little limewater. If the gas is carbon dioxide, the limewater turns milky (cloudy). This is a very reliable test because no other common gas turns limewater milky.

The milkiness is a fine white solid. Carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide to form calcium carbonate, which is insoluble in water, so it appears as a suspension of tiny white particles: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l). Calcium carbonate is the same compound found in chalk and limestone.

Carbon dioxide is produced in many reactions. Carbonates react with acids to form a salt, water and carbon dioxide, for example CaCO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). Many metal carbonates decompose when heated, for example CuCO₃(s) → CuO(s) + CO₂(g). The complete combustion of fuels containing carbon, such as methane, produces carbon dioxide and water. Respiration in living things and fermentation of sugar by yeast also release carbon dioxide.

A burning splint goes out in carbon dioxide, but this is not a valid test for carbon dioxide on its own, because other gases such as nitrogen also put out a flame. Carbon dioxide is colourless, odourless and denser than air. It dissolves slightly in water to form a weakly acidic solution, so it turns damp blue litmus slightly red, but the AQA test that identifies it is the limewater test.
keyFacts: Limewater is an aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂.
Test: bubble the gas through, or shake it with, limewater.
The milkiness is insoluble calcium carbonate: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O.
Carbonate + acid → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
Thermal decomposition of metal carbonates produces carbon dioxide.
Complete combustion of carbon-containing fuels, respiration and fermentation produce carbon dioxide.
A flame going out is NOT a valid test for carbon dioxide.

keyTerms.definition: A clear, colourless aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, used to test for carbon dioxide.
The appearance of limewater when a fine white precipitate of calcium carbonate forms in it.
An insoluble solid formed when two solutions (or a gas and a solution) react.
CaCO₃, an insoluble white solid that forms when carbon dioxide reacts with limewater.
Breaking down a compound using heat, for example copper carbonate → copper oxide + carbon dioxide.

equations.name: Limewater reaction
equations.formula: calcium hydroxide + carbon dioxide → calcium carbonate + water

equations.formula: calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide

workedExamples.title: Identifying the gas from marble chips
workedExamples.question: Marble chips (calcium carbonate) are added to dilute hydrochloric acid. Bubbles of gas form. Name the gas and describe how to show it is this gas.
steps: Carbonate + acid → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
Pass the gas through limewater using a delivery tube.
Observe whether the limewater changes from clear to milky.
workedExamples.answer: Carbon dioxide; it turns limewater milky (cloudy).

workedExamples.title: Explaining the milkiness
workedExamples.question: Explain why limewater turns milky with carbon dioxide. Include a balanced equation.
steps: Carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide to make calcium carbonate and water.
Calcium carbonate is insoluble, so it forms a fine white precipitate that makes the liquid look milky.
workedExamples.answer: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l); the insoluble CaCO₃ makes it cloudy.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often write that carbon dioxide 'puts out a lighted splint', as the test.
misconceptions.right: In fact many gases put out a flame. The test that identifies carbon dioxide is that it turns limewater milky.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often say limewater turns 'milky white' and then 'precipitate of calcium hydroxide'.
misconceptions.right: In fact the white solid is calcium carbonate; calcium hydroxide is what is dissolved in limewater.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think limewater is a solution of lime juice or citric acid.
misconceptions.right: In fact limewater is a solution of calcium hydroxide, which is alkaline.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think carbonates produce hydrogen with acids like metals do.
misconceptions.right: In fact carbonates react with acids to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide.

realWorld: Breathing out through a straw into limewater shows that exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air.
Fire extinguishers use carbon dioxide because it is denser than air and does not support combustion.
Limestone buildings react with acid rain, releasing carbon dioxide and slowly wearing away.
examTips: Write 'limewater turns milky' or 'cloudy'. 'Limewater turns white' alone may not be accepted; never say it 'turns clear'.
Give limewater's chemical name, calcium hydroxide solution, if asked what it is.
If asked which reaction produced a gas that turns limewater milky, think: carbonate + acid, heating a carbonate, combustion, respiration or fermentation.
For 'describe the test' questions give both the method (bubble through limewater) and the result (turns milky).
summary: Bubble or shake the gas with limewater.
The cloudiness is insoluble calcium carbonate.
Carbonates with acid, heated carbonates, combustion and respiration all produce CO₂.

questions.question: Which reagent is used to test for carbon dioxide?
markScheme: 1 mark: Limewater
questions.explanation: Limewater (calcium hydroxide solution) is the test for carbon dioxide. The others test for ions.

questions.question: What is the positive result of the limewater test?
markScheme: 1 mark: Limewater turns milky
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky (cloudy) because a white precipitate forms.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of limewater?
markScheme: 1 mark: Calcium hydroxide solution
questions.explanation: Limewater is calcium hydroxide dissolved in water. Calcium carbonate is the insoluble product that forms.

questions.question: What is the white solid that makes limewater milky?
markScheme: 1 mark: Calcium carbonate
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O. Calcium carbonate is insoluble so it forms a fine suspension.

questions.question: Which reaction produces carbon dioxide?
markScheme: 1 mark: Sodium carbonate with hydrochloric acid
questions.explanation: Carbonate + acid → salt + water + carbon dioxide. The other reactions produce hydrogen, hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.question: Why is a burning splint going out not a good test for carbon dioxide?
options: Carbon dioxide makes a splint burn brighter
The splint relights in carbon dioxide
Several other gases also put out a flame
markScheme: 1 mark: Several other gases also put out a flame
questions.explanation: Nitrogen and other gases also extinguish flames, so this result does not identify carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which equation shows the reaction of limewater with carbon dioxide?
markScheme: 1 mark: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O
questions.explanation: Calcium hydroxide reacts with carbon dioxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate and water.

questions.question: Green copper carbonate is heated strongly and the gas is passed into limewater. The limewater turns milky and a black solid remains. What is the black solid?
markScheme: 1 mark: Copper oxide
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition: CuCO₃ → CuO + CO₂. Copper oxide is black.

questions.question: Which of these processes does NOT release carbon dioxide?
markScheme: 1 mark: Photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide and releases oxygen. The other three release carbon dioxide.

questions.question: A student breathes out through a straw into limewater. What happens and why?
options: Nothing, because exhaled air has no carbon dioxide
Limewater turns blue, because exhaled air is acidic
Limewater turns milky, because exhaled air contains oxygen
Limewater turns milky, because exhaled air contains carbon dioxide from respiration
markScheme: 1 mark: Limewater turns milky, because exhaled air contains carbon dioxide from respiration
questions.explanation: Respiration produces carbon dioxide, so exhaled air turns limewater milky. Oxygen does not affect limewater.

questions.question: Describe the test for carbon dioxide and give the result.
markScheme: 1 mark: bubble the gas through / shake with limewater
1 mark: limewater turns milky / cloudy
questions.explanation: Both method and result are required.

questions.question: Name the gas produced when a metal carbonate reacts with a dilute acid.
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Carbonate + acid → salt + water + carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Explain why limewater turns milky when carbon dioxide is bubbled through it.
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide (in limewater)
1 mark: to form insoluble calcium carbonate / a white precipitate
questions.explanation: The insoluble solid particles scatter light, making the liquid look milky.

questions.question: Write a word equation and a balanced symbol equation for the reaction of calcium carbonate with hydrochloric acid.
acceptedAnswers: calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide
markScheme: 1 mark: calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide
1 mark: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂
questions.explanation: Calcium ions are 2+, so 2 HCl are needed to form CaCl₂.

questions.question: Write a balanced symbol equation for the complete combustion of methane, CH₄, and state how you could show that one of the products is carbon dioxide.
markScheme: 1 mark: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
1 mark: pass the gases through limewater, which turns milky
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon gives carbon dioxide and water; the CO₂ is identified with limewater.

questions.question: Write a balanced symbol equation, with state symbols, for the reaction that makes limewater milky.
markScheme: 1 mark: correct formulae Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O
1 mark: correct state symbols (aq), (g), (s), (l)
questions.explanation: The (s) for calcium carbonate shows it is the precipitate responsible for the cloudiness.

questions.question: A student heats zinc carbonate in a test tube connected to a tube of limewater. Predict the observation in the limewater and name both products of the reaction.
markScheme: 1 mark: limewater turns milky
1 mark: zinc oxide and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Metal carbonates thermally decompose to the metal oxide and carbon dioxide: ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂.

questions.question: What colour is limewater before carbon dioxide is added?
markScheme: 1 mark: clear / colourless
questions.explanation: It changes from clear to milky when carbon dioxide is present.

questions.question: A student has two test tubes of colourless gas. One contains carbon dioxide and the other contains nitrogen. Both gases put out a burning splint. Describe how the student could identify the carbon dioxide, and explain why the burning splint test cannot tell them apart.
markScheme: Indicative content: bubble/shake each gas with limewater
Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky (cloudy)
Nitrogen has no effect; limewater stays clear
Milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms
Both gases do not support combustion, so both put out a flame
So the splint test gives the same result for both
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct test and results for both gases plus explanation of why the splint test fails
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): limewater test or result given
questions.explanation: Only the limewater test is specific to carbon dioxide.

questions.question: A student is given a white powder that is thought to be a metal carbonate. Describe two different ways the student could produce a gas from the powder and show that the gas is carbon dioxide. Include balanced equations, using calcium carbonate as the example, and explain the result of the test.
markScheme: Indicative content: Method 1: add dilute hydrochloric acid to the powder; fizzing
CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂
Method 2: heat strongly (thermal decomposition)
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
Pass gas through limewater with a delivery tube (or shake with limewater)
Limewater turns milky
Explanation: CO₂ reacts with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate
Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O
Safety: remove delivery tube from limewater before stopping heating to avoid suck-back; eye protection
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): both methods clear, correct test and result, at least two correct balanced equations, explanation of milkiness
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): one method with test and result, some equations or explanation
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): basic statement of limewater test or one method
questions.explanation: The best answers include both routes to CO₂ with balanced equations and explain the chemistry of the limewater test.

questions.question: Yeast is added to sugar solution in a flask connected to a tube of limewater. After a day the limewater is milky. Which process produced the gas?
markScheme: 1 mark: Fermentation
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar to ethanol and carbon dioxide; the carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.

questions.question: Which gas turns limewater milky?
markScheme: 1 mark: Carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Only carbon dioxide gives this result.

questions.question: Four gases are bubbled through limewater and tested with damp litmus. Which gas turns limewater milky and does not bleach the litmus?
markScheme: 1 mark: Carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky. Chlorine bleaches damp litmus. Hydrogen and oxygen have no effect on limewater.

questions.question: A student uses old limewater that has been left open to the air for a week. It is already slightly cloudy before the test. Suggest why, and explain why this would make the test unreliable.
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon dioxide from the air has reacted with the limewater, forming calcium carbonate
1 mark: so a change to milky would be hard to see / the result is unclear
questions.explanation: Limewater should be fresh and clear so that a positive result is obvious.

questions.question: Suggest one reason why carbon dioxide can be collected by downward delivery (into an upright tube).
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon dioxide is denser than air, so it sinks into the tube and pushes the air out
questions.explanation: Gases denser than air collect at the bottom of an upright container.

questions.question: Indigestion tablets containing magnesium carbonate react with stomach acid (hydrochloric acid). Which products form?
options: Magnesium chloride, water and carbon dioxide
markScheme: 1 mark: Magnesium chloride, water and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Carbonate + acid → salt + water + carbon dioxide: MgCO₃ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Hydrogen forms from metals (not carbonates) with acid; magnesium oxide forms when the carbonate is heated.
